What are the Kankakee County due dates?

The 2026 bills were payable in two installments, the first due June 25, 2026 and the second due September 3, 2026. Taxes in each bill relate to the previous assessment year, so the bills payable in 2026 were based on finalized 2025 assessed values.

Late payments carry a penalty of 1.5 percent per month, which matches 35 ILCS 200/21-15 for a county with fewer than 3,000,000 residents. The treasurer's calendar adds a deadline for paying by personal check without a newspaper publication fee, a mailing of delinquent notices, and a last day to pay in the office, and it states that the annual tax sale for delinquent properties takes place in November each year. The treasurer's office can give exact dates.

Can Kankakee County owners spread out their payments?

Yes. The treasurer runs a voluntary program called CHOICES that lets an owner prepay on a weekly or monthly schedule instead of waiting for the two due dates. It is meant for owners without mortgage escrow, and there is no penalty if a planned payment is skipped.

Fees for the program are $1 per electronic check and 2.25 percent plus $1.50 for credit cards. Payments can be made online, by mail, or in person at the treasurer's office or its drop box, but not at a bank. The program does not stop the 1.5 percent monthly charge on any balance left after a due date, and the full installment must be paid by each date to avoid interest. There is no discount for paying early. Anyone who sells a house mid-year should ask the treasurer how prepayments will be applied to the current bill.

What is the way to contest a Kankakee County assessment?

File an assessment appeal with the Kankakee County Board of Review on the county's 2026 Assessment Appeal Form, after speaking to your township assessor. The Supervisor of Assessments page lists the 2026 publication and appeal deadline dates, the Board of Review rules and procedures, and the form itself.

The Board of Review rules and procedures are posted on the same page. The board decides the assessed value of any appealed parcel based on the evidence presented at a public hearing. Deadlines run from the publication date of each township's assessment changes, which differ across the county's seventeen townships, so look up your township before you plan. Ask the Supervisor of Assessments at (815) 937-2945 for the date that applies to your parcel.

Which exemptions does Kankakee County list?

The Supervisor of Assessments office lists applications for homestead relief, and the Treasurer's calendar says exemptions must be filed by March 1 each year. Senior and disability exemptions are handled through the assessor.

  • General and Senior Homestead Exemptions, with a combined application.
  • Senior Assessment Freeze, form PTAX-340, with separate forms for the 2025 bill payable in 2026 and the 2026 bill payable in 2027.
  • Disabled Person (PTAX-343) and the Physician's Statement (PTAX-343-A), plus an application for a Disabled Person ID Card.
  • Disabled Veteran (PTAX-342) and Returning Veterans exemptions.
  • Homestead Improvements, for added value from a new improvement.

Dollar limits for each program are on the county forms, so open the form for the exemption you want before you count on a reduction.

What did the March 2026 storm change for Kankakee County owners?

Homes damaged in the March 10, 2026 storm can be reviewed by the assessor, but no storm reduction could be applied to the 2026 bills. The county explained that bills payable in June and September 2026 were based on 2025 assessed values, which reflect the 2025 calendar year.

Owners with storm damage, or a home that is uninhabitable, should contact the township assessor or the Supervisor of Assessments so the property is reviewed for the 2026 tax year. The Natural Disaster Homestead Exemption under 35 ILCS 200/15-173 may apply after the structure is rebuilt. The county lists these requirements:

  • The structure must be rebuilt within two years of the disaster.
  • The rebuilt square footage may not exceed 110 percent of the original.
  • The first application is due no later than the first taxable year after the rebuild.
  • The exemption must be applied for each year.

What do owned homes in Kankakee County look like?

For 2020 to 2024 the typical Kankakee County owner-occupied home was valued at $192,600, and owners live in 69.9 percent of homes. Renters pay a median $1,097, and the household income median is $71,281. The county has 45,655 housing units and 40,996 households.

Owners report $1,649 a month with a mortgage and $718 without one. Builders pulled 113 permits in 2025, and one resident in five is past 65. Anyone selling a home with deferred repairs or storm damage should check the taxes owed and the exemptions in place first.

What local landmarks affect a sale in Kankakee County?

Olivet Nazarene University and Kankakee Community College sit in the county, and the Kankakee Amtrak station carries the Illini and Saluki trains to Carbondale and the City of New Orleans. The Greater Kankakee Airport serves the county, and River Valley Metro runs local transit in the city while SHOW Bus covers Momence and rural areas.

Winters are cold, with a January average low of 12 degrees and a record low of minus 29 recorded in January 1985. Summers average highs of 86 degrees in July.

Pay the County Treasurer at 189 East Court Street in Kankakee, phone (815) 937-2960. The counter is open on weekdays, and the treasurer's site shows the payment season.

What does a late Kankakee County payment cost?

Late installments accrue interest at 1.5 percent per month. Taxes still owing at the annual November tax sale can be offered at that sale.

Where do Kankakee County seniors apply for relief?

Apply through the Supervisor of Assessments at (815) 937-2945. The treasurer's calendar says exemption filings are due by March 1 each year, and the county posts the senior, disabled person and veteran forms.

Can I appeal my Kankakee County assessment?

Yes. Speak to your township assessor first, then file the county's assessment appeal form with the Board of Review within the deadline listed for your township.

Is there help with storm damage on my Kankakee County house?

Contact your township assessor or the Supervisor of Assessments so the property can be reviewed for the 2026 tax year. The natural disaster exemption may apply once the home is rebuilt, within two years and no more than 110 percent of the original size.

How is Kendall County laid out for someone selling a house?

Kendall County is a small, fast-growing county in the Chicago area, with Yorkville as county seat and Oswego as its most populous village. It was formed in 1841 out of LaSalle and Kane Counties and covers 322 square miles, with the Fox River running through the northwest. Most residents live in the northeast and along that river, while the south stays largely agricultural.

Two moraines cross at Oswego Township and raise some northern ground above 800 feet.

Who handles property tax in Kendall County?

Three county offices and the township assessors share the work, and the county lists 504 S. Main St in Yorkville, IL 60560 for the Treasurer and the assessment office. Offices close for county holidays.

  • Township assessor: explains how your assessment was determined. The phone number is on the back of the tax bill.

Start with your township assessor, then file a written complaint with the Board of Review inside 30 days of publication. The 2026 final filing date was October 19, 2026, and the filing window closes on the 30th day after publication for each township each year.

The Board of Review has three members appointed by the County Board, and each member must pass a state examination. The board reviews assessments made by township assessors, adds omitted property, hears complaints, and can raise or lower an assessment on its own motion. It also equalizes assessments between townships and reviews petitions for tax exemption, then passes its list of valuations to the County Clerk to compute tax rates. Complaint forms, instructions and the board's rules for 2026 are available by calling (630) 553-4146.

How does Kendall County bill, and what does a late payment cost?

  • The minimum charge for a bounced check is $25.00, and the payment is voided.
  • The county does not mail the original bill to a mortgage company, so an owner should ask the lender whether it needs a copy.
  • A duplicate bill is free to the owner, and non-owners pay $5.00.

Payments on the wrong parcel cannot be refunded automatically. Ask the Collector at (630) 553-4124 for the installment dates printed on your bill.

How do I protest a Kendall County tax bill?

To protest a bill, pay the tax in full and file a tax objection complaint with the Kendall County Circuit Clerk, and then the tax counts as paid under protest. No protest form or note on the bill is needed at the time of payment.

The Treasurer's protest letter sets two clocks, both counted from the first penalty date of the second installment. Full payment is due by day 60, and the complaint by day 75. For the 2025 tax year the letter gives November 9, 2026 for payment and November 24, 2026 for the complaint. The Circuit Clerk's fee is $119.00 for the first parcel and $50.00 for each added parcel. An objection to the assessed value requires that you first filed an assessment complaint with the Board of Review, and a filing with the state Property Tax Appeal Board for the same year blocks it. The letter notes that the Kendall County tax sale has generally been held in late October, so full payment must come before the sale to keep a property off it.

Which exemptions does Kendall County offer?

  • Home Improvement Exemption: up to $75,000 of added value for four years, certified by the township assessor with no application.
  • Senior Citizen Homestead Exemption: a $5,000 reduction for owners 65 or older, with a yearly renewal form mailed by the office.
  • Senior Assessment Freeze: household income cap of $65,000, yearly application, due on or before September 1.
  • Returning Veterans: a $5,000 reduction for two consecutive years.
  • Disabled Veterans' Standard Exemption: $2,500 for a 30 to 49 percent rating, $5,000 for 50 to 69 percent, and the first $250,000 of assessed value exempt at 70 percent or more.
  • Disabled Persons: a $2,000 reduction, with an annual application.

Religious, charitable and educational groups apply for non-homestead exemption through the Board of Review.

What do owned homes in Kendall County look like?

A seller can use the county's tax bill search to check the amount owed on a parcel before listing. The Collector at (630) 553-4124 can confirm what is unpaid.

The northern half of the county falls in Community College District 516, served by Waubonsee Community College in Sugar Grove, Aurora and Plano, and the southern half is in District 525 with Joliet Junior College. Interstate 88 and Interstate 55 improved commuting to Chicago after World War II and fed the suburban growth that followed.

Silver Springs State Fish and Wildlife Area is the only designated state park in the county. A rural parcel can carry farmland assessments, which the 2026 notice increased by $56.71 per acre for each soil productivity index. Ask the township assessor which class your land is in.

Is there a Kendall County senior freeze?

Yes, for owners 65 and up whose household income is $65,000 or less. The county wants the application by September 1 every year.

Knox County by the numbers

Who handles property tax matters in Knox County?

A seller in Knox County will typically touch three offices. The County Treasurer, based in the courthouse in Galesburg, mails the bills and takes the money. The county Assessment Office, 309-345-3845, runs exemptions and hands out Board of Review forms. Township assessors set the values. Tax sale certificates and redemption sit with the County Clerk.

Assessing is split three ways. One assessor covers the North District: Rio, Ontario, Walnut Grove, Lynn, Henderson, Sparta, Copley, Victoria, Persifer and Truro townships. Another covers the South District: Galesburg, Knox, Cedar, Orange, Haw Creek, Elba, Indian Point, Chestnut, Maquon and Salem. The City of Galesburg township has a separate assessor of its own, so the right call depends on the parcel's location.

How large is Knox County and what do homes sell for?

Knox County takes in 716 square miles of land in west central Illinois, and Galesburg is both the seat and the biggest city. Fulton County gave up land to create it in 1825. It borders Mercer, Henry, Stark, Peoria, Fulton and Warren Counties. Among the ten school districts are Galesburg CUSD 205, Knoxville CUSD 202 and ROWVA CUSD 208.

The population is sliding: 49,967 in the 2020 count and an estimated 47,767 in July 2025. Census figures for 2020 through 2024 show a $111,900 median home value, 70.8% of households owning their homes and a median income of $57,030. One building permit was issued in 2025, and 23.9% of residents are 65 or older.

Where values are this low, a modest bill still eats a real share of a house's worth, so look at the assessment before you list.

What are the Knox County tax due dates and late penalties?

Taxes for the 2025 tax year were payable in 2026 on two dates, July 1 and September 1. Both dates have passed. Knox County mails one bill a year with a detachable stub for each installment, so check the dates printed on the current bill or ask the Treasurer.

Knox County late penalty on 2025 taxes payable in 2026 (source: Knox County Treasurer, Important Dates)

Per the Treasurer, the charge is 1.5% each month, applies in full rather than by the day, and begins the morning after a due date. Not getting a bill does not excuse the tax (35 ILCS 200/20-15).

Where can you pay a Knox County tax bill?

The Treasurer offers several ways to pay, and the detachable stub has to go with the payment:

  • Send a check or deliver it to the Treasurer's Office, made out to Knox County Collector; a mailed check's cancelled copy is your receipt
  • Leave a check in a courthouse drop box, one on Tompkins Street by the north curb and one at the parking lot exit, with no envelopes supplied
  • Take it to a local bank in the county (Wells Fargo is excluded at its own request)
  • Use a credit or debit card and pay a fee of 2.35%, with a $2.95 minimum

A postmark counts if the payment goes out before the tax sale. Drop box items collected at 8:30 each morning are posted to the day before. Where a lender pays from escrow, the county puts the duty of watching those payments on the owner.

How is a Knox County assessment determined?

Assessors value property as of each January 1, aiming for 33.33% of fair cash value and drawing on three years of sales; the 2026 roll used 2023 through 2025. Equalization factors follow. In 2026 they were 1.0724 in Galesburg Township, 1.0758 for the City of Galesburg, 1.0132 in Rio, Walnut Grove, Henderson and Persifer, and 1.0125 in Ontario, Sparta and Copley. Lynn, Truro, Victoria, Elba and Salem were general assessment townships that year.

The county's formula for a bill takes the final equalized assessed value, subtracts exemptions, and multiplies what remains by the tax rate. To test your own figure, divide the assessment by 0.3333 and compare that with a realistic sale price.

Before the 2026 adjustments, the three-year median assessment level measured 32.92% in the North District, 31.08% in the South District and 31.76% in the City of Galesburg, which is why the factors above push values upward. Farmland follows a separate state formula, and its factor was 1.00.

What is the Knox County assessment appeal process?

First talk to the township assessor. If that does not settle it, put a written appeal in front of the Board of Review. It must argue the property's value, not the size of the tax. Knox County's 2026 filing period ran September 17 through October 19, 2026, ending at 4 p.m., and it is over. Each year brings new forms, and older ones are refused.

  • Support the appeal with facts, such as an independent appraisal or sales of comparable homes
  • The Board answers with a notice carrying an informal decision
  • To contest it, return your acceptance of a formal hearing within ten days of the notice
  • Thirty days after a final Board decision is the limit for going to the Property Tax Appeal Board

The Board of Review meets as needed rather than on a fixed calendar. For the current forms and window, call the Assessment Office.

What exemptions apply to a Knox County home?

Exemption forms and instructions live on the county's assessment pages, and the Treasurer's page summarizes the main ones:

  • Owner-occupied homestead: a reduction of up to $6,000 in equalized assessed value
  • Senior homestead for owners 65 and older: $5,000 off
  • Senior assessment freeze: holds the taxable value for owners 65 and older; the Treasurer lists household income of $65,000 or less, and the assessment office shows $75,000 for 2026
  • Home improvement: assessed value of up to $25,000 exempt for four years

Other exemptions cover returning veterans, disabled persons and disabled veterans. Applications are requested by September 30 yearly and accepted until December 31. A buyer who moves in should contact the assessment office after the next January 1 to confirm the exemption is on the parcel.

What happens to delinquent Knox County taxes?

Knox County runs one tax sale a year, usually in mid-November, and every delinquent tax is offered. A list of delinquent taxes is printed in local newspapers each mid-October. Beginning with the 2025 taxes payable in 2026, the county chose under Public Act 104-0553 to acquire all delinquent real estate taxes itself as trustee for the taxing districts. That trustee then auctions parcels it has taken to deed.

Tax sale certificates are handled by the County Clerk's Office, 309-345-6753. The Treasurer will not give legal advice about delinquent taxes. Anyone who sells with tax outstanding should ask the Treasurer what is owed and settle it at closing.

More questions about Knox County, IL Property Tax Guide

What dates does Knox County collect real estate tax?

The 2025 taxes payable in 2026 were due July 1 and September 1, 2026. The Treasurer mails one annual bill with a stub for each installment, so read the dates on your own bill.

What late fee does Knox County charge?

The Treasurer adds 1.5% per month to the unpaid amount, with no proration, starting the day after a due date.

Is the 2026 Knox County appeal period still open?

No. It ran from September 17 to October 19, 2026, and the Board of Review may not accept complaints afterward. Call the Assessment Office at 309-345-3845 about the next window.

Where do I send a Knox County property tax payment?

The Treasurer's Office in the Knox County courthouse in Galesburg takes mail and walk-in payments. Drop boxes, most local banks and card payments are also options, and checks go to the Knox County Collector.

When does Knox County hold the tax sale?

Lake County by the numbers

Who does what on property tax in Lake County?

Lake County property tax runs through several offices, each with its own question. The Treasurer (847-377-2323) mails the bills, collects payment and passes the money to the districts. The Chief County Assessment Office supervises values, with township assessors doing the local work. Appeals go to the Board of Review. The County Clerk works out the rates and takes over after a tax sale for redemption.

With 18 townships in the county, your township assessor is where a worry about the number on your assessment notice should start. Little of what you pay stays with the county: Lake County government gets about seven percent of an average bill, and school districts take about 69 percent. More than 200 separate taxing bodies levy tax here.

How big is Lake County and what do homes cost there?

Lake County fills the northeast corner of Illinois, touching Wisconsin and Lake Michigan, and Waukegan serves as seat and largest city. Its total area is 1,368 square miles, yet 444 of them are land. No other Illinois county has more water than land.

Residents numbered 714,342 at the 2020 Census, and the July 2025 estimate is 719,339. For 2020 through 2024 the bureau lists a $345,700 median home value, 74.8% of homes lived in by their owners, and $110,416 in median household income. Permits for 1,468 new units came in 2025. Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $2,503, so a bill of several thousand dollars a year is a real line item.

The county lists dozens of cities and villages and many separate elementary and high school districts, so the mix of taxing bodies depends on the parcel. The district maps and the bill itself show which ones apply.

How does the Lake County property tax cycle work?

One cycle spans two years, which means a bill reflects work done the year before. In year one, township assessors set values as of January 1 at one third of fair market value, using three years of sales. The county then equalizes values across townships, mails assessment notices known as blue sheets, and the Board of Review hears appeals. Taxing districts pass budgets and levies during the same year.

In year two, the Board finishes its hearings, the County Clerk figures tax rates from the levies and the final values, and the Treasurer mails bills at the start of May. The county's warning is blunt: by the time you get the bill, it is too late to protest it. The time to speak up is at the assessment notice and at the budget meetings of the taxing districts.

What is the Lake County property tax payment schedule?

Bills arrive in early May, with installments in June and September. The Treasurer's calendar for tax year 2025, collected in 2026, lays out the sequence:

Lake County 2025 real estate tax calendar, payable in 2026 (source: Lake County Treasurer, Real Estate Tax Calendar)

November 12Last day to pay to avoid tax sale, by 5:00 p.m., no postmark
November 13Tax sale

The county says the due dates, interest dates and the tax sale date are fixed, while other dates on the calendar may shift for administrative reasons.

What does a late Lake County payment cost, and can you prepay?

Under state law the collector adds 1.5% a month to any unpaid installment, figured on the 5th of the month with no proration. For the 2026 collection, a first installment paid between June 5 and July 4 carried 1.5%, and by the October 5 to November 12 window it reached 7.5%. The second installment started at 1.5% on September 5 and reached 3.0% in the last window.

  • Not receiving a bill, medical emergencies and travel do not qualify for forgiveness of the penalty
  • Forgiveness applies only to a documented Lake County error
  • In the final weeks before the sale, the Treasurer's Office takes only cash or certified funds, in person
  • A December prepayment window lets owners pay up to 50% of the previous year's bill, by check only, with the parcel number in the memo line

Owners who pay through mortgage escrow can look up status on the Treasurer's site by parcel number, though a payment can take weeks to appear as paid.

How does an assessment appeal work in Lake County?

Each township has its own deadline, which falls one month after its assessments are published. The 2026 final filing dates ran from August 24 for Benton and Ela townships to November 2 for Shields. Waukegan's closed September 8, Libertyville's September 21 and Antioch's October 19, and all of those have passed.

The Board urges a conversation with the township assessor beforehand and requires one for factual-error appeals. Appeals are filed online through the Smartfile system. The county names these reasons as typical:

  • A factual error such as the wrong square footage
  • An assessment above one third of the recent sale price
  • An assessment above one third of market value
  • An assessment higher than comparable properties

You may choose a hearing by letter, phone, in person or Zoom, and corporations and LLCs must use an attorney. Hearings are finished in early February. A missed window forfeits the appeal for that year.

Which exemptions reduce a Lake County tax bill?

Exemptions are filed through the Smartfile e-filing portal run by the Chief County Assessment Office, and staff will help by phone or in person.

  • General homestead: takes $8,000 off equalized assessed value for an owner's main residence as of January 1, with no yearly renewal
  • Senior exemption: another $8,000, which can be claimed on top of the general homestead
  • Senior assessment freeze: protects limited-income seniors from increases from rising values, but not from higher tax rates
  • Senior tax deferral: lets qualified seniors defer part or all of the tax on their residence
  • Home improvement, disabled persons and veterans exemptions

Exemptions do not transfer to a newly assigned parcel number, so a split or combined lot needs a fresh application under the new number.

What happens to unpaid Lake County taxes at the tax sale?

By law the Treasurer sells each year's unpaid taxes, and the sale falls in November after October final notices. The county stresses that the house itself is not sold, just the delinquent taxes. A tax buyer pays them, the districts receive the money, and the owner then works with the County Clerk's Office on redemption.

A seller who owes tax should clear it by closing. The Treasurer can quote the amount due, the County Clerk can estimate redemption for a parcel already sold, and the Treasurer's Office also handles payment status, delinquent prior-year taxes and duplicate bills.

What are the Lake County, Illinois property tax due dates?

Bills are mailed in early May with installments in June and September. For tax year 2025 the dates were June 4 and September 4, 2026.

How much is the penalty on a late Lake County tax payment?

State law adds 1.5% per month to an unpaid installment, counted on the 5th and never prorated. Forgiveness is limited to documented Lake County errors.

What is the deadline to contest a Lake County assessment?

One month after your township's assessments are published. In 2026 those dates ranged from August 24 to November 2, depending on the township, and all have passed.

Does Lake County sell the house at the tax sale?

No. Only the unpaid taxes are sold, and the owner then redeems through the County Clerk's Office.

Is there a way to prepay Lake County property tax?

Yes, during a December window announced by the Treasurer. Prepayment may be up to 50% of the prior year's bill, by check only, with the parcel number in the memo.

Who do you contact about a Lee County tax bill?

Four desks inside one courthouse in Dixon split the job. Questions about value or exemptions belong with the assessment staff, payment trouble goes to the Treasurer, and a question about how a rate came out goes to the Clerk's extension department.

County Clerk and RecorderExtends rates, takes redemption money after a sale, records deeds815-288-3309, mailing box 329

The Treasurer reports collecting and passing along more than $96 million this year to over 130 taxing districts. That explains why a Lee County bill reads like a ledger of school, township, fire and county lines rather than one charge.

What should a seller know about Lee County itself?

Lee County lies along the Rock River country of northern Illinois and was carved out of Ogle County on February 27, 1839. Dixon, where Ronald Reagan spent part of his boyhood, is the seat and the biggest city. Amboy is the other incorporated city the county lists, while Rochelle lies mostly across the line in Ogle County. Land area is roughly 725 square miles, and the neighbors are Ogle, DeKalb, LaSalle, Bureau and Whiteside.

The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 32,914 people, a drop from the 34,145 counted in 2020. Of occupied homes, 73.6% have owners living in them. The midpoint value for an owner-occupied home in the 2020 to 2024 survey is $154,600, and the midpoint household income is $70,292. Builders took out just 32 permits in 2025. An EF4 tornado touched down here on April 9, 2015, so storm history is a fair question for a buyer.

Several school districts cut across the county, including Dixon Unit 170, Amboy 272, Ashton 275, Lee Center 271, Polo 222 and Sterling 5. Whichever one serves your address drives much of the rate.

How are Lee County homes valued for tax?

Township assessors propose values, and the county assessment office pulls them together. The target for houses is one-third of fair cash value. When a single parcel changes, the office mails a notice. When the only change comes from a township-wide equalization factor, no notice is required.

Illinois runs on a four-year general reassessment. The county's publication page names Amboy, Ashton, Bradford, Franklin Grove, Nachusa, Lee Center, May and Sublette as the townships in their general year for 2026. Anyone can look over a parcel's size, age, lot and sketch at the assessment counter, or search property record cards on the county site.

A bigger bill does not always mean a bigger assessment. The county's FAQ gives three general explanations: a taxing district asked for more, an exemption you qualify for has not been applied, or other owners picked up exemptions you lack. The county itself can only set its own levy. Under the state's extension limitation law, most districts may grow their levy by the smaller of 5% or inflation over the highest of the prior three years, and new construction, bonds and referendum-approved increases sit outside that cap.

What is the process to contest a Lee County value?

You file a written complaint with the Board of Review within 30 calendar days of the assessment list being published, as 35 ILCS 200/16-55 requires. For the townships named above, the county lists November 18, 2026 as the publication date and December 18, 2026 as the last day to file. Townships not on that list have their own publication dates, so ask the assessment staff which applies to you.

Three members, chosen by the County Board, sit on the Board of Review, and they may confirm, lower or raise a value. The county's FAQ says its rules accept these grounds:

  • Equity, meaning your value out of line with similar homes
  • Fair cash value
  • A wrong physical description of the property
  • Questions of law

Speak with your township assessor or the county staff beforehand, since many disputes end in that conversation. After the 30 days, only a physical-data mismatch, such as a house recorded larger than it is, can still be raised. If the Board's ruling disappoints you, the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board takes the next step at 217-782-6076 or 401 S Spring Street, Room 402, Springfield. The Board looks at value only, so an objection to the size of the final bill belongs with the taxing districts.

How do you pay Lee County real estate tax?

The state splits the bill in two, and the county prints each due date on the bill itself. Under 35 ILCS 200/21-15, a first installment turns delinquent after the later of June 1 or the day following the printed date. The second follows the same test against September 1. Late interest is 1 1/2% for each month or fraction. A mailed payment with a postmark on or before the date counts as on time.

Ways to pay include:

  • The county's property tax inquiry website, which shows a pay link after you search by PIN, owner name or address.
  • Phone payment at 877-690-3729 with jurisdiction code 7042.
  • A check mailed to Lee County Collector, P.O. Box 328, Dixon, IL 61021.
  • The Treasurer's counter at the Old Lee County Courthouse.

The county's due-dates page states a 2.40% card fee through a third party with a $2.00 floor. For e-checks it prints $2 up to $50,000, then $4, $8.50 and $10 in higher bands. If you never received a bill, ask the Treasurer for a duplicate, since a missing bill does not cancel the debt. Send address updates on the county's change-of-address form.

Which Lee County breaks reduce a bill?

An exemption subtracts from equalized assessed value ahead of the rate. Because Lee County does not border a county with 3,000,000 or more residents, the lower statutory ceilings apply. These are the main ones:

  • General homestead: a reduction of as much as $6,000 on a home the owner lives in (35 ILCS 200/15-175).
  • Senior citizens: as much as $5,000 once the owner turns 65 within the assessment year (35 ILCS 200/15-170). The county's form says the exemption renews on its own after approval, and owners must tell the office if the home stops qualifying.
  • Senior freeze: a yearly application, with household income held under the limit on the county form.
  • Tax deferral: the Treasurer's program for owners 65 and over whose household income is at most $75,000, moving to $77,000 for tax year 2026 and $79,000 for 2027. The postponed tax rides as a lien until the house sells.

File exemption forms with the assessment office. After a sale, state law keeps the seller's homestead credit through the assessment year of the sale, and the office can ask the buyer to apply for the year after.

What if the Lee County bill goes unpaid?

What gets sold is the unpaid tax, not your home. Each year the Treasurer puts every unpaid parcel into a tax sale. You keep the right to redeem by paying the tax with added costs and interest, and the redemption desk sits in the County Clerk's office.

State law usually gives three years from the sale date, subject to exceptions in 35 ILCS 200/21-350. If a buyer already holds a certificate on your parcel, get the Clerk's payoff figure and final date in writing before you set a price or sign a contract.

How do taxes settle at a Lee County closing?

A title agent or attorney reads the latest bill, checks for installments still open, and divides the year between seller and buyer on the closing statement. Before that, ask the Treasurer whether any older year is delinquent or sold, since that balance must be cleared at the table. When a lender escrows taxes, find out which installments it has remitted.

Houses that come with probate, tenants or deferred repairs often carry back taxes too. A payoff letter from the Treasurer, together with a redemption figure from the Clerk if a sale happened, lets you weigh competing offers on equal terms.

Which number reaches the Lee County Treasurer?

815-288-4477 for bills and payments. The assessment office at 815-288-4483 takes value, exemption and appeal questions, and the Clerk's extension department at 815-288-3309 explains how rates are built and handles redemption.

Is there any way to appeal late in Lee County?

Only for a physical-data error. The county's FAQ says complaints must come within 30 days of the roll's publication, with the single exception of a mismatch like the wrong square footage on the record.

What is the largest general homestead reduction in Lee County?

$6,000 of equalized assessed value, since the county does not border one with 3,000,000 or more inhabitants. The rule is 35 ILCS 200/15-175, and the assessment office takes the application.

What does late payment cost in Lee County?

Interest of 1 1/2% per month or partial month under 35 ILCS 200/21-15. The clock starts after the later of the statutory date or the day after the printed due date, and a timely postmark avoids it.

Does Lee County's senior deferral wipe out the tax?

No, it only delays it. The deferred amount becomes a lien and comes due when the house is sold. An applicant must be 65 or older and apply through the Treasurer, whose page states the income limit.

What is Logan County like for a homeowner?

Logan County is central Illinois farm country with Springfield, Bloomington, Peoria and Decatur all within reach. Lincoln is the seat. The state created the county in 1839, and in 1845 it took in a slice of De Witt County to reach today's outline of roughly 618 square miles of land. Mason, Tazewell, McLean, De Witt, Macon, Sangamon and Menard counties surround it.

Lincoln, the biggest city, was founded in 1853 along the Chicago and Mississippi Railroad and is described as the first city named for Abraham Lincoln while he was still a lawyer. Atlanta and Mount Pulaski are the county's other two cities. I-55 connects Lincoln with Bloomington and Springfield, Amtrak calls at Lincoln Station, and the Logan Correctional Center stands near the city in unincorporated territory.

Lincoln averages about 26 degrees in January and about 75 in July, with 126 days a year below freezing. Roof, gutter and foundation condition are the usual points a buyer's inspector checks on a house like this.

Which Logan County desks deal with tax, and where are they?

The Treasurer's page splits the duties among three Lincoln offices.

  • Supervisor of Assessments (122 N. McLean St., 217-732-9635): directs the township assessors, maintains tax maps and parcel record cards, grants exemptions and acts as clerk to the Board of Review.
  • County Clerk (courthouse Room 20, 217-732-4148): applies each levy to the assessed base to produce rates, and handles redemption of tax sale certificates.
  • County Treasurer (courthouse Room 11, 217-732-3761): sends bills, takes payments, logs granted appeals and distributes the money.

The Treasurer doubles as county collector for real estate, mobile home and drainage tax. All owners pay county, township and road and bridge tax. Schools, fire protection and other districts layer on top, and your rate depends on which boundaries enclose your parcel.

What did the 2025 Logan County tax calendar look like?

The county's Treasurer page lays out the 2025 tax year, collected in 2026. All of these dates are behind us, and the same pattern comes round each year with fresh dates.

  • Real estate bills went in the mail May 8, 2026.
  • The first installment fell due June 15, 2026 and the second September 1, 2026, each carrying a 1.5% monthly penalty if missed.
  • Mobile home bills were mailed March 30, 2026 and were due June 1, 2026, with a $25 penalty after that day and another $25 each month, capped at $100.
  • The tax sale took place October 29, 2026 at 9:00 a.m., and buyer registration closed October 16, 2026.

Under Public Act 104-0553, the page says, Logan County chose to acquire delinquent real estate taxes as trustee for the taxing districts. When a due date slips past, the Treasurer asks owners to phone for the up-to-date amount because penalty keeps growing.

Where can you pay Logan County property tax?

Bring the payment stub from your bill whichever route you pick. The Treasurer lists these:

  • The counter in courthouse Room 11, with cash or check. A card works for real estate tax only, at a charge of 2.35% plus $1.50.
  • The drop box on N. Kickapoo St. facing Latham Park, or the boxes on the courthouse's north and south sides. No cash in the boxes.
  • Most banks in the county, except Regions and CEFCU.
  • Mail, where the postmark is honored as the date received.
  • Card or e-check by phone at 217-203-8359 with the property index number, or through the link on the Treasurer's page.

A bill you never received is still owed. State law counts a mailed payment as timely when postmarked by the due date, and the first installment turns delinquent after the later of June 1 or the day after the printed date (35 ILCS 200/21-15).

How is a Logan County bill built from the assessment?

Township and county assessors set the assessed value, then the abstract goes to the state, which can add a multiplier that moves values up, down or not at all. The County Clerk takes each district's levy, divides it by that district's assessed valuation, and arrives at a rate, held to any statutory cap. The combined rate times the equalized assessed value is your tax.

Assessment level is one-third of market value. The Supervisor of Assessments applies equalization factors to hold that level, and the Board of Review rules say every parcel is reassessed on a four-year cycle, though yearly reassessment is allowed. The 2026 preamble and publication ran in the Lincoln Courier on Friday, October 2, 2026, and a PDF copy is linked from the office's page.

The Supervisor's office also registers mobile homes. Taxes must be current and the title valid first, and a Treasurer's tax certificate is needed to move a title at the Secretary of State.

How does a Logan County owner contest a value?

Per the Board of Review rules, the window is 30 days from publication of assessment changes in your township. Complaint and evidence must be at the assessment office by 4:30 p.m. that day or be mailed with a postmark on or before it. A chat with the assessor does not stop the clock.

The rules include several traps:

  • One complaint per parcel, on the Board's own form. Faxed and emailed complaints are refused.
  • One copy of your evidence goes in with the form. A form that says no evidence provided will likely return a decision of no change.
  • Only the assessment can be protested, never the amount of tax.
  • If something is missing, you get a notice and 10 days to supply it.
  • Hearings are by appointment, last about 15 minutes, and take no new evidence.

Three members appointed by the County Board make up the Board, and it convenes by the first Monday of June. Owners get a written tentative decision and must ask for a hearing within the time printed on it.

What exemptions does the Logan County assessment office offer?

The office's page lists the following, and staff check eligibility, sometimes asking for proof every year:

  • Owner-occupied homestead: $6,000 off assessed value for people who live in the home they own.
  • Senior citizen: a further $5,000 once the owner reaches 65, with proof of age.
  • Senior freeze: holds the value at the first qualifying year for owners already on the senior exemption, with household gross income of $65,000 or less in assessment year 2025 and $75,000 or less from 2026.
  • Homestead improvement: shelters the added value from a garage, porch or deck on an owner-occupied house for four years.
  • Returning veterans: $5,000 off the main residence for two straight years.
  • Veterans with disabilities: $2,500 at a 30 to 49% service-connected rating, $5,000 at 50 to 69%, and full exemption at 70% or above.
  • Persons with disabilities: $2,000, renewed with annual proof.

The statutes agree on the first two dollar amounts for a county that does not border one with 3,000,000 or more people (35 ILCS 200/15-175 and 15-170).

What should a Logan County seller do about taxes before closing?

Look up your parcel on the county's tax search, set it beside the bill you hold, and phone the Treasurer for what is owed on any open installment. The title company divides the year between seller and buyer, and the settlement statement shows what is paid, due or held in escrow. A lender that escrows taxes can confirm what it has already sent.

Prior years that went unpaid make for a harder sale. Ask the County Clerk whether the taxes were sold and what redemption costs, since a certificate holder has to be paid before title is clear. The statute usually allows three years from the sale date, with exceptions (35 ILCS 200/21-350).

Which number do I call at the Logan County Treasurer's office?

217-732-3761. The office is in Room 11 of the courthouse in Lincoln, and the Treasurer's page sends owners with questions about a bill or a past-due amount to that number.

How big is the late charge on Logan County real estate tax?

The Treasurer's page says 1.5% per month is added when an installment is unpaid by its due date. Mobile home tax draws $25 after June 1, then $25 more each month up to $100.

Does the Logan County Treasurer accept cards?

Yes, for real estate tax. Options are the counter, the phone line at 217-203-8359 and the online link, and the page states a 2.35% plus $1.50 fee for card payments at the counter. Have your property index number ready.

What is the appeal window for a Logan County assessment?

Thirty days from publication of changes for your township. The complaint, with evidence, must be in by 4:30 p.m. or postmarked by that day, and every parcel needs its own form.

Where do I apply for the homestead exemption in Logan County?

At the Supervisor of Assessments, 122 N. McLean St. in Lincoln, or by phone at 217-732-9635. The office's page describes the owner-occupied exemption as $6,000 off assessed value.

Macon County by the numbers

What is Macon County, Illinois, and where do you pay its tax?

Macon County is the Decatur area of central Illinois. It was formed January 19, 1829 from Shelby County and named for Nathaniel Macon. Decatur is the seat and the biggest city, with Macon and Maroa as the other two cities. The land is flat, left that way by the Pleistocene ice sheet, and the county likes to be called the Heart of Illinois. Its neighbors are De Witt, Piatt, Moultrie, Shelby, Christian, Sangamon and Logan counties, and the Lincoln family arrived in 1830.

The Treasurer mails roughly 55,000 bills a year, money that funds schools, libraries, parks, cities and the county. The office sits in the Macon County Office Building, 141 South Main Street, Room 302, Decatur, phone 217-424-1426, open 8:30 to 4:30 on weekdays except legal holidays. Online payment runs through maconcountyil.us, and the site's help desk can be reached at 844-400-8880.

What does the Census say about homes in Macon County?

The population estimate for July 1, 2025 is 99,300, which is 4.5% under the April 2020 base, and 83.0% of residents lived in urban areas at the 2020 count. The county makes up the Decatur metropolitan area.

Decatur's January lows average near 17 degrees and July highs near 88, so heating, roofing and drainage are fair questions for any older house.

Who sets value in Macon County, and how can you look it up?

The Supervisor of Assessments, at 141 South Main Street, Room 401 (217-424-1364, open 8:30 to 4:30 on weekdays), supports the township assessors, runs exemptions, maintains the parcel maps and record cards, applies equalization factors and publishes assessments in local papers. The same office is clerk to the Board of Review.

Outside Cook County, Illinois aims for 33 1/3% of market value. To see your number, use the county website, a mailed notice if the parcel changed or the township is in its general year, the newspaper publication, your tax bill, or a phone call. Property record cards print for $.35 a page by address or PIN, and sales transfer declarations are open for viewing at the office, handy if your appeal rests on comparable sales.

The final bill equals assessed value less exemptions, times the rates of every district serving the parcel. A house one block over can sit in a different mix of districts, so a neighbor's bill is a weak yardstick.

When did the 2026 Macon County appeal period end?

The county's 2026 notice names October 10, 2026 as the publication date for 2026 assessments and November 9, 2026 as the last day to file with the Board of Review. That window is over. The standing rule is 30 calendar days after publication, townships have separate publication dates, and the county's FAQ says state statute bars any appeal after the deadline.

The Board has three members, appointed by the County Board. It hears between 800 and 1,000 appeals in a tax year and usually wraps up hearings by the end of February. The county's FAQ names the evidence that helps:

  • A realtor's market analysis
  • A certified appraisal
  • A grid of comparable properties
  • The closing statement from a purchase
  • Photos

You argue either equity, comparing assessments on similar nearby homes, or market value, which requires recent sales. The Board has no say over the tax bill, so a hearing built only on high taxes goes nowhere.

What comes after a Macon County Board of Review ruling?

The Board is in session from June 1 and writes by mail only, so double-check the mailing address on your complaint. Replies come in three forms: the Board accepts your numbers, it sends its own tentative value and gives you 10 days to request a hearing in writing, or it sets a hearing date that can be moved once.

A final notice generally arrives in January. You then have 30 days from its postmark to go to the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board, where the case starts over and fresh evidence is welcome. Beyond that lies court, and the county advises consulting an attorney. The Board also acts on property left off the roll, and must notify the owner first.

What are Macon County's installment dates and late penalty?

Bills go out in May. Installment one falls due 30 days after the mailing date. Installment two is September 1, shifting to the next working day when that lands on a weekend or on Labor Day. The county bills a year behind, so what you pay in one calendar year covers the previous tax year. Expect a single bill with two tear-off coupons, never a second mailing.

The Treasurer's page says state statute demands a penalty of 1 1/2% for every month or fraction after the due date, even if a payment is a single day late, and tells owners to call for the exact amount. A bill that never shows up does not erase the debt. If a mortgage servicer pays from escrow, check with it to avoid paying twice or not at all.

Mobile homes follow another schedule. Bills are mailed in April, the full tax is due within 60 days, and afterwards $25 a month or fraction accrues up to $100. Selling or moving a mobile home requires a $10 tax certification.

How does a Macon County tax sale unfold?

Once second-installment posting is complete, a certified delinquent notice goes to the billing address, with $10 added for mailing and newspaper publication. The Treasurer also prints the owner's name, parcel number and amount due in a county paper. Unpaid tax then goes to the annual sale, where tax buyers bid interest downward from 9%, and the lowest bidder gets the certificate. What is purchased is the tax, never the house.

The Treasurer's page puts redemption for an owner-occupied home at no less than 30 and no more than 36 months, paid at the County Clerk's office. The payoff covers the tax sold, penalty, publication, sale costs, the buyer's other costs and interest bid up to 9% compounded every six months. The statute generally allows 3 years from the sale, with exceptions (35 ILCS 200/21-350), so ask the Clerk for the date that governs your certificate.

Which breaks can a Macon County owner use, and what changes at a sale?

Macon County does not border a county with 3,000,000 or more people, so the lower statutory homestead amounts apply. The general homestead exemption is up to $6,000 off equalized assessed value (35 ILCS 200/15-175), and the senior exemption is up to $5,000 for an owner 65 or older who lives in the home (35 ILCS 200/15-170). The Supervisor of Assessments handles the paperwork.

The Treasurer runs the Senior Citizens' Real Estate Tax Deferral Program. The Supervisor of Assessments separately accepts affordable housing applications under 35 ILCS 200/10-260 by September 1 of the assessment year.

At a sale, let the title company settle who owes which installment. A new owner should send the Treasurer a change of address form by March 15, since the address on a recorded deed reaches that office only after a delay.

More questions about Macon County, IL Property Tax Guide

Where can I pay a Macon County tax bill?

Online at maconcountyil.us or at the Treasurer's counter, 141 South Main Street, Room 302, Decatur. For bill questions call 217-424-1426, and for payment site trouble call 844-400-8880.

Is the 2026 Macon County appeal period still open?

No. It ended November 9, 2026. The county gave October 10, 2026 as the 2026 publication date, and the rule allows 30 calendar days from publication.

Does Macon County send a second bill for the later installment?

No. Owners get one bill a year with two coupons, and the second installment is due September 1, or the next working day when that falls on a weekend or Labor Day.

Do I lose my Macon County house at the tax sale?

Not at the sale. Tax buyers purchase the unpaid tax, and the owner can redeem by paying the redemption amount at the County Clerk's office.

What is the fee for mobile home tax certification in Macon County?

$10, payable by cash or check only. Taxes must be paid to date, the original title must be shown, and the Treasurer needs the names and addresses of seller and buyer.
